mechanics.text: Core loop: the player character stands in a small arena facing a stationary target dummy. Pressing a single 'Punch' input (default: left mouse click or gamepad face button A / keyboard Space) triggers a punch action if the player is not already mid-punch (no input buffering/combo chaining in this version). The punch action plays a forward jab animation on the player rig, lasting roughly 0.3-0.5 seconds total (windup, strike, recovery). A hit is registered when the punch's active strike frame overlaps the dummy's hitbox (simple capsule or box collider on the dummy's torso). On a successful hit: (1) a punch/impact sound effect plays once, (2) the on-screen hit counter increments by exactly 1, (3) the dummy may play a small reactive flinch/wobble animation for feedback (non-damaging, purely cosmetic), (4) a brief cooldown prevents a second increment from the same punch swing (one hit registered per animation cycle, even if overlap persists across multiple frames). The dummy has no health, cannot be defeated, and never attacks back; it simply resets to idle pose after each flinch. The counter persists for the duration of the play session and resets to 0 on scene reload/restart. A 'Reset Counter' input or UI button is provided for convenience. Player movement is limited to basic forward/back/strafe (WASD or left stick) within the arena bounds so the player can position themselves at punching range from the dummy; no jumping or blocking mechanics are included in this scope.
assumptions: Single-player only; no multiplayer, AI opponent behavior, or networking.
Dummy is purely stationary and cannot be damaged, destroyed, or knocked over; it exists only as a hit target.
Only one punch type/animation is required (no combos, kicks, blocks, or special moves) per the request scope.
Hit counter is a simple integer displayed as on-screen UI text (e.g., 'Hits: 0') anchored to a screen corner.
Counter increments exactly once per successful punch connection, regardless of overlap duration, using a per-swing hit-registered flag.
Default control scheme: WASD/left-stick for movement, one button (Space/left-click/gamepad A) for punching.
No scoring, timer, win condition, or difficulty progression is required; this is a practice/demo loop, not a scored game mode.
Punch and hit use the same single sound effect (no separate whiff vs. connect sounds) unless later expanded.
Player character and dummy are simple humanoid rigs; exact art style is defined in the theme section.
Camera is a fixed third-person or side-view camera framing both the player and dummy at all times; no free camera control needed.

theme.text: A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
assumptions: Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.

environment.text: Layout is a small, enclosed rectangular gym room (roughly the size of a single boxing ring plus a bit of walking space), viewed from a fixed side or three-quarter camera angle so both the player and the dummy remain visible on screen at all times. The target dummy is anchored to the floor near the center-right of the play space; the player spawns a few steps to the left, within comfortable punching range after a short walk/strafe. Simple background elements (gym mats, a wall, maybe a window or poster) provide visual context without requiring complex level geometry. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed screen-space position (e.g., top-center or top-right) so it remains visible during gameplay regardless of camera framing. Arena boundaries (invisible walls or a mat edge) keep the player from wandering away from the dummy, ensuring the punch target is always reachable.
assumptions: Single static scene/level; no level transitions, multiple rooms, or loading between areas.
Play space is small enough that the dummy is always within a few steps of the player spawn point, avoiding any need for a minimap or waypoint guidance.
Lighting is simple ambient/static lighting (no dynamic day-night cycle or complex lighting rigs).
No destructible or interactive environment props beyond the dummy itself in this scope.
